messages:
Maya: Heads-up — Silverline Labs renewal in ~6 weeks and they dropped API activity ~45% WoW. Procurement pinged us that they're running a cost-focused bakeoff with VendorX. Need a quick triage: usage root cause, competitive ask, and next steps. @Diego can you pull contract commits and any recent procurement notes?

Diego: On it. Quick summary: 12 seats, committed ~500k tokens/month at current tier. Procurement requested a POC from VendorX last Thursday. I also saw Finance flagging last month's overage charge on the bill.

Ravi: I'll start with telemetry — could be auth/SDK changes or a client-side throttling experiment. If errors spiked they'd reduce calls. Running a quick query now: ```sql
SELECT date_trunc('day', ts) as day, sum(api_calls) as calls, sum(errors) as errors
FROM usage
WHERE account_id='silverline'
  AND ts > now() - interval '30 days'
GROUP BY 1
ORDER BY 1 DESC;
```

Maya: Thanks. Also Olivia (their PO) said in the last touchpoint they were unhappy with sudden token overage and wanted a lower flat-rate option. She also mentioned VendorX demo showed similar latency.

Olivia: quick note from our side — we paused a lot of bulk export jobs last week to stabilize costs, which explains part of the drop. But leadership is definitely sensitive to the monthly bill variability. VendorX pitched a predictable monthly price that looks ~20% cheaper on paper.

Diego: Got it. So it's a mix: deliberate export pause + procurement price pressure. Need both a technical remediation (to avoid accidental pauses) and a commercial counter.

Ravi: Telemetry shows error rate unchanged but a spike in 429 throttles from March 6–7 between 02:00–06:00 UTC. Also several clients switched to our older SDK which has a batching regression. That could explain reduced throughput. Action: I'll draft a short SDK patch and a config we can ship to their engineers.

Maya: Good catch. For commercial: propose a two-track response: 1) short-term win: offer a 2-week Dedicated pilot (no charge) to prove steady latency and a fixed-rate invoice simulation; 2) mid-term: present a tailored pricing model or bill credit for last month's overage. Thoughts?

Diego: Sales is ok with a pilot if we get a formal POC scope and success criteria. Procurement wants SOC2 + SOC2 bridge and SSO SAML cert details before any pilot. procurement-bot: Please attach the standard SOC2 + SSO checklist.

procurement-bot: Attached: SOC2 cert (redacted), standard SSO checklist, sample PO terms.

Olivia: Procurement will need the SOC2 docs. CTO also wants a short perf bench comparing VendorX on their 1k–5k concurrent users scenario. If Redwood can show better 99th p99 latency under that load, they'll lean our way.

Ravi: I'll run a focused perf bench on Dedicated simulating 1k–5k concurrent users and capture p50/p95/p99 and cost per 1k tokens. Deliverable: 1-page perf summary + raw numbers. ETA: 48 hours.

Maya: I'll coordinate the enablement session for Silverline's devs — 45 min runbook: SDK bump, batching best practices, prefix caching. Also prepare a one-pager cost comparison (VendorX vs current bill + proposed Dedicated pilot sim).

Diego: I'll draft a short commercial offer: 2-week Dedicated pilot credit, a one-time bill credit up to $X for overage (TBD by Finance), and a readiness checklist. I can escalate discount approval if needed.

Maya: Action items summarised: 
- Maya: schedule enablement + produce cost one-pager (due EOD tomorrow).
- Ravi: perf bench + SDK patch + 1-page perf summary (48h).
- Diego: draft POC scope & pilot commercial terms, coordinate with Finance/procurement (48h).
- Procurement: confirm SOC2 + SSO checklist received (ASAP).

Olivia: Appreciate the fast response. I'll push for a decision window after the pilot and share their internal procurement timelines tomorrow.

Maya: Cool — will set a 30-min sync for tomorrow 10am PT to align and share deliverables. :thumbsup: :eyes:

Ravi: Noted — will post bench results in the thread.

Diego: Adding a brief note to CRM and flagging renewal risk.

Maya: Thanks team — let's keep replies concise in this thread so we have a single source of truth for the POC.

(reacts: :thumbsup: by Diego, :eyes: by Ravi)
